steward: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (NLS program; documentation at nlsinfo.org)
population: All biological children of female NLSY79 respondents (NLSY79 women were 14-21 on 31 Dec 1978); with weights, representative of children born to that national sample of women, not of a U.S. birth cohort
age_coverage: Child assessments biennially 1986-2014 for children under 15; Young Adult interviews from age 15 (from 2016, age 12+); 2020 YA ages 12-50
baseline_n: 1986: 5,255 children born to 2,922 interviewed mothers; 4,971 children interviewed. 11,551 children identified as born to NLSY79 mothers (cumulative). 2020: 4,354 Young Adults interviewed
waves: Child: 1986, 1988, ..., 2014 biennial (16 child rounds through 2020 incl. limited 2016/2018 mother reports); Young Adult: 1994-2020 biennial (14 rounds)
adult_support_measures: HOME-SF (mother report + interviewer observation) with age-specific Parts A (0-2), B (3-5), C (6-9), D (10-14), emotional-support subscale; identical mother-report items in Parts C and D (child's closeness to mother/father, praise, physical affection, past week); child self-report (ages 10-14, CSAS, 1994-2014) closeness to each parent, parent talks over decisions, listens, shares ideas, monitoring; child report of teachers ('Most of the teachers are willing to help with personal problems', age 10+, 1988-2014); YA closeness to mother/father (2000 younger YAs; all YAs from 2002)
adult_education_outcome: Yes: HGC_DLI, HSTDEGREEDLI (cross-round), HGCyyyy (2004-2020), HSTDEGREEyyyy (2012-2020), degree-specific completion flags and dates
survey_design: Children of a multi-stage national household sample with Black and Hispanic oversamples; cross-sectional child weights CSAMWTyyyy (and _REV), YA weights YAyyWEIGHT; custom weights available; military and economically disadvantaged non-Black/non-Hispanic oversamples dropped
access: Public-use data free via NLS Investigator (account only needed to save datasets); restricted geocode via ResearchDataGov Standard Application Process (U.S.-based researchers only); zip/tract files only at BLS or FSRDCs (none for YA)
major_limitations: Sample is defined by mothers, so child birth year is confounded with maternal age at birth (early-born children have young mothers) and the cohort is not representative of U.S. children of any single birth year; HOME parts change at age 10 (not at 12), and only a subset of items repeat across Parts C and D, while total/subscale raw scores contain different items by age; child self-report of parenting begins at 10, so no child-report measure at 8-9; HOME not administered after 2014; YA over 30 interviewed every other round from 2010

dataset: PSID Child Development Supplement (original CDS 1997/2002/2007) + Transition into Adulthood Supplement (TAS)
steward: Panel Study of Income Dynamics, Survey Research Center, Institute for Social Research, University of Michigan
population: Children aged 0-12 in 1997 in PSID families (up to two per family), nationally representative U.S. family panel incl. 1997 immigrant refresher
cohort_birth_years: 1984-1997 (original CDS); ongoing CDS (2014+) covers children born since 1997
age_coverage: CDS-I 1997 ages 0-12; CDS-II 2002-03 ages 5-18 (user guide; TAS-2023 guide says 5-17); CDS-III 2007-08 ages 10-19 (CDS-III guide; TAS guide says 10-17); TAS ages 18-28; core PSID thereafter
baseline_n: CDS-I: 3,563 children in 2,394 families (88% response; 2,380 child households in response-rate section); CDS-II: 2,907 children (2,019 families, 91%); CDS-III: 1,506 children (90%); TAS-2005: 745 aged 18-20; TAS-2023: 2,434 completed of 2,793 eligible (87% RR), 13.4% original CDS members
waves: CDS 1997, 2002-03, 2007-08; TAS 2005-2015 biennial (original CDS cohort), 2017+ steady-state biennial (all PSID members 18-28); core PSID biennial
adult_support_measures: PCG-reported Parental Warmth (CDS-I G37a-f; CDS-II/III E13a-g with 2 items dropped and 3 added); HOME-SF; child-reported (ages 8+ in CDS-II; 10+ in CDS-III) closeness to mother, father, stepparents, favorite teachers, other adults outside school (H5a-h) and who the close adults are incl. mentor, coach (H6); child-reported talk with mother/father (H4); TAS retrospective closeness/affection with parent before 18 (H53-H55, ACE neglect subscale)
adult_education_outcome: Yes: TAS G5 grade completed (e.g., TA230990), constructed Enrollment Status (TA232392, 10 statuses incl. 4-yr grad), degree items; core PSID individual-file YEARS COMPLETED EDUCATION (e.g., ER34548 for 2017)
survey_design: Embedded in the national PSID household panel (genealogical design); CDS/TAS cross-sectional and longitudinal weights (TAS-2023 guide ch. 6)
access: Free; registration required to download CDS/TAS via the CDS-TAS Data Center; restricted data (e.g., geocode) require application with IRB-approved data protection plan (FAQ: doctoral-level faculty, others case by case)
major_limitations: Only two child self-report waves (2002, 2007) five years apart, so within-person contrast of ~8-11 vs ~12-15 exists only for children aged ~8-10 in 2002 (born ~1992-1994): small subsample; CDS-I child interview did not include closeness items; PCG warmth items changed between CDS-I and CDS-II; age at each wave varies by birth year (age and period confounded within cohort); attrition 3,563 -> 1,506 by CDS-III (partly by design: aged-out children)
verification_status: verified via psidtest.isr.umich.edu mirror PDFs (psidonline.isr.umich.edu blocked 403); variable names verified from codebooks

dataset: Future of Families and Child Wellbeing Study (FFCWS; formerly Fragile Families)
steward: Princeton University and Columbia University; public data via Princeton OPR data archive and ICPSR 31622
population: Births in large U.S. cities (population >200,000), 20 cities; births to unmarried mothers oversampled 3:1; national weights apply to 16 randomly selected cities
baseline_n: 4,898 children (stratified multistage sample); Year 9: 3,515 mothers; Year 15: 3,580 PCGs and 3,444 teens; Year 22: 2,990 young adults (61% of baseline) and 2,744 PCGs
adult_support_measures: Child self-report from age 9: 'How close do you feel to your mom/dad?' and 'How well do you and your mom/dad share ideas or talk about things that really matter?' asked at Year 9 (k5a2e/k5a2f), Year 15 (k6c17/k6c18) and Year 22 (k7e5/k7e6); Year 9 teacher survey (social skills etc.; no relationship scale found); Year 15 school climate (teachers care) and non-parental adult confidant (k6c40/k6c41); Year 22 parent-like figure incl. teacher (k7e19_13, k7e23)
adult_education_outcome: Yes at ~22: k7b1 highest grade/degree; ck7edu constructed (less than HS / HS / some college / college or grad); restricted National Student Clearinghouse degree fields (rs7nsc_*)
survey_design: Stratified multistage city-birth sample; national and city weights
access: Most data free (public); restricted contextual/linked data (prefix (RES), source 'restricted') require a restricted-use contract data license (metadata site); ffcws.princeton.edu and ICPSR returned 403 from this machine so registration terms are unverified
major_limitations: Only one wave in each developmental window (age 9 vs age 15), so no within-window repeated measures and 15 is at the upper edge of 12-15; child report starts at 9 (none at 8 or 10-11); outcome at ~22 precedes typical BA completion (age 22-25), so attainment is right-censored; urban, non-marital-birth oversample, not national; Year 22 response 61% of baseline; single birth cohort so no age-period separation
verification_status: verified (DataCite record for ICPSR 31622 and FFCWS metadata explorer CSV); official ffcws.princeton.edu pages not reachable (403)
sources: https://api.datacite.org/dois/10.3886/icpsr31622 (DataCite metadata of ICPSR 31622 landing page https://doi.org/10.3886/ICPSR31622); https://metadata.ffcws.princeton.edu/ (FFMetadata_v22_f.csv via /get_metadata); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fragile_Families_and_Child_Wellbeing_Study (secondary, used only for corroboration)

dataset: NICHD Study of Early Child Care and Youth Development (SECCYD)
steward: NICHD (study complete; funding ended 2009); data archived at ICPSR series 233
population: Diverse sample of children and families enrolled in 1991 at 10 U.S. sites (not nationally representative)
age_coverage: Phase I 0-3 (1991-94); Phase II 54 months-1st grade (1995-99); Phase III 2nd-6th grade (2000-04); Phase IV 7th-9th grade / age 15 (2005-07)
waves: Four phases 1991-2007 with annual or more frequent assessments
adult_support_measures: Teacher-reported Student-Teacher Relationship Scale (STRS; Pianta) in Phase III (2nd-6th grades per instrument chart; also in Phase II chart); mother/father-reported Child-Parent Relationship Scale short form (Phase III and age 15); child-reported 'Getting Along with My Parent' (parental warmth, support and hostility; 6th grade and age 15); HOME inventory; Network of Relationships Inventory
adult_education_outcome: No (not in the NICHD-documented phases, which end at age 15); any adult follow-up is unverified
survey_design: Purposive multi-site hospital-birth recruitment; no population weights documented on fetched pages
access: Via ICPSR series 233 (ICPSR returned 403 here; restricted-use status and DUA terms unverified)
major_limitations: No adult educational attainment in documented phases; single birth year; not nationally representative; ICPSR access terms unverified; instrument grade timing read from a scanned chart layout and needs confirmation in ICPSR codebooks
verification_status: partially verified (NICHD pages and phase instrument PDFs); ICPSR documentation unreachable (403)

population: Nationally representative sample of kindergartners in public and private schools, 1998-99
cohort_birth_years: unverified - needs manual check (kindergarten entrants in fall 1998)
baseline_n: 21,260 kindergartners participated in the base year; 21,409 children responding in any round (K-8 child catalog)
waves: Fall and spring K (1998-99); fall (30% subsample) and spring 1st grade (1999-2000); spring 3rd (2002); spring 5th (2004); spring 8th (2007)
adult_support_measures: Teacher and parent questionnaires each round; child self-description (SDQ) and NELS:88 Self-Concept and Locus of Control scales at 8th grade; item-level adult-support measures not verified in this audit
survey_design: Nationally representative multistage school-based sample; cross-sectional and K-8 longitudinal weights with replicate weights (e.g., C7CW0)
access: K-8 longitudinal public-use file; restricted-use data require an NCES restricted data license and are released only as grade-level cross-sectional files
major_limitations: No outcomes after 8th grade, so cannot test any hypothesis about adult educational attainment; only one measurement in 12-15 window (8th grade, ~age 14); no verified repeated relationship scale
verification_status: verified for design and N (nces.ed.gov); item-level support measures unverified

population: Nationally representative sample of children in kindergarten in 2010-11 (first-time and repeating kindergartners)
adult_support_measures: Teacher-reported Student-Teacher Relationship Scale (STRS, Pianta) closeness and conflict composites, kindergarten through 3rd grade (X2/X4/X4K/X6/X7 CLSNSS and CNFLCT); child self-report SDQ I
survey_design: Nationally representative multistage sample; weights per manual
access: Public-use K-5 file; restricted-use license via NCES for restricted files; STRS and other instruments copyright-protected
major_limitations: Ends at 5th grade (~age 11); STRS only K-3 (~ages 5-9), so covers neither the full 8-11 window nor any of 12-15; no adult outcomes
verification_status: verified (nces.ed.gov manual NCES 2019-051 and K-5 record layout)

population: Around 19,000 young people born across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
baseline_n: around 19,000 (CLS page; exact baseline count unverified)
adult_support_measures: Parenting, relationships and family life tracked (CLS page); item-level measures at 11 and 14 unverified - needs manual check
adult_education_outcome: Age 23 sweep exists; specific education variables unverified
survey_design: UK birth cohort; design details not reviewed
access: Free of charge, mostly via UK Data Service; some data via CLS Data Access Committee
major_limitations: UK school system and credentials not directly comparable to U.S. attainment; item-level comparability at 11 vs 14 not verified

steward: UCL Centre for Longitudinal Studies (formerly UK Department for Education)
population: Around 16,000 people in England in Year 9 in 2004 (original sample 15,770 recruited through schools; deprived schools oversampled by 50%)
access: Free of charge, mostly via UK Data Service
major_limitations: Starts at age 13-14, so it cannot measure the 8-11 window (same problem as U.S. adolescent-start cohorts)
